_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for LMT retrospectives (retro/build_lmt.py), generated from the converted rows of Lockheed Martin's filings (every figure read from its labelled row, the row asserted present in its own filing). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2006-2026 were accepted before the open on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it) and the latest declared dividend (else the vintage's). Lockheed Martin's fiscal year is the calendar year. EPS is diluted EPS (from continuing operations where reported), each year from the latest 10-K that reports it; FY2002 is excluded (unusual items larger than its earnings, no per-share figure excluding them), so the history and the P/E window start with FY2003 ('pe_window_start'). A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', $ millions; the builder re-derives and checks them), each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it; backlog against the year-ago quarter's end as that quarter's own release shows it ('backlog_prior_source'). From 2010 a print takes diluted EPS from continuing operations where the release reports the line, and a release that republishes earlier years' EPS restates them until a later 10-K ('restates', EPS only; the Q4 2016 release's FY2015 without IS&GS). From the FY2013 vintage ('why_themes') the builder ends the durability 'why' with every live theme's reading as of AS_OF, from the vintage's own words ('cloud_words', 'climate_words', 'oil_words'). From 2018 (retro/README.md, "LMT 2018-2021"): a year whose GAAP EPS fails the AAPL FY2002 test takes the company's figure from the latest filing that publishes one (2017, the Tax Act), a release may restate it ('restates'), a guide may carry the restated base the release states beside it ('rev_base_usd_b'), and a guide given with and without an announced item takes the figure without it. Guides: the fiscal-year outlook table's current column (net sales and diluted EPS ranges, a level stated as about read as a number, words keeping the last numeric range; segment operating profit and cash from operations are display only: no margin is derived from two guided figures), and the third-quarter release's preliminary outlook for the next year. Rule T's raw figures are in 'rule_t'. From 2022 (retro/README.md, "LMT 2022-2026"): the company's adjusted EPS removes recurring mark-to-market items (2021-2023) or results of programs in performance (2024), so GAAP stands; an outlook that includes a booked one-off with no figure without it stands as published; from 2023 segment operating profit excludes intangible asset amortization, each print against the year-ago quarter as its own release recasts it; the FY2023-FY2025 10-Ks supply their three income-statement years and the segments' summed year-end backlog; GENAI and GLP1 are read as out of scope from each vintage's own words ('ai_words'; 'climate_words' and 'weather_words' from the FY2021 10-K).

rule_t._doc: Rule T over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04): each annual change from the latest 10-K published by then that tabulates both years, as tabulated. Backlog is total negotiated backlog at year-end and net sales the five-year summaries' (the FY1998-FY2000 10-Ks' backlog charts; seams stay in: discontinued operations restate 1999 and 2000 backlog and net sales in later 10-Ks). Segment operating profit and the segment margin ('Total business segments' operating profit on the table's total net sales) are tabulated on the recast basis of the 8-K of 2003-01-16 (unusual items, the FAS/CAS pension adjustment and stock-based compensation outside the segments) from the FY2002 10-K, so they have 2001-2006 (the AVGO rule): the FY1998-FY2001 10-Ks report segments that include unusual items and pension income, with a Corporate and Other segment, a different measure. EPS is the FY2006 history's (2004-2006: FY2002 is excluded and the history starts with FY2003; the F and SO rule)
